title: Exponential growth & decay
examples: When does the graph get very close to the x axis?
How do I find the time for something to become half its size?
Can you show me an example of population growth?

explain.say: Today we look at exponential change using the form y equals a base to the x.
This model describes things that grow or shrink by a fixed percentage over time.
For growth, the base a must be greater than one. Think of bacteria multiplying quickly.

items: Base a must be greater than one

explain.say: For decay, the base a must be between zero and one. Radioactive material decays over time.

items: Base a between zero and one

explain.say: The half-life tells us the time it takes for a substance to reduce to half its initial amount.
Imagine a small population of rabbits that grows by ten percent each month. This growth follows an exponential pattern. The initial number is the starting point for the calculation.

faq.q: What is the difference between exponential growth and decay?
faq.a: Growth means the value gets bigger by a constant factor over time. Decay means the value gets smaller by a constant factor over time.
asks: How do I tell if it is growing or shrinking?
What does the base number tell me about the change?

faq.q: What does the asymptote mean on a graph?
faq.a: An asymptote is a line that the graph gets closer and closer to but never actually touches. It shows a limit.
asks: Why does the graph approach a line?
Is the asymptote the value the graph reaches?

faq.q: How do I use the half-life concept?
faq.a: You use the half-life when the decay rate is given as a fraction of the original amount. You divide the original amount by two repeatedly.
asks: Do I calculate the decay rate from half-life?

faq.q: Does the base 'a' always have to be positive?
faq.a: Yes, in these standard models, the base a must always be a positive number. Negative bases create complex patterns not usually covered here.
asks: Can I use negative numbers in the base?
What happens if a is zero?

faq.q: If y equals a base to the x, what does the x represent?
faq.a: The x usually represents the time that has passed or the number of intervals that have occurred. It is the independent variable.
asks: What is the role of the x variable?

facts: Exponential growth means the rate of change increases as the value increases.
Exponential decay means the rate of change decreases as the value decreases.
The line y equals one is a horizontal asymptote for most decay models.
The half-life is the time required for a quantity to reduce to half its initial size.

quiz.why: The base zero point five is less than one, which shows decay.

wrong.1: This base is greater than one, which shows growth.
wrong.2: This is a linear equation, not an exponential one.
wrong.3: This structure does not fit the standard exponential form.

quiz.say: If a substance has a half-life of two hours, what happens after four hours?

options.show: It will be one quarter of the original amount.
options.say: It will be one quarter of the original amount.

options.show: It will be half the original amount.
options.say: It will be half the original amount.

quiz.why: After two hours it is half, and another two hours it is half of that, making one quarter.

wrong.1: This only accounts for one half-life period.
wrong.2: It approaches zero but never actually reaches it.
wrong.3: The concept here is decay, not growth.

quiz.say: What is the horizontal asymptote for the function y = 10 (0.8)^x?
quiz.why: As x gets very large, the value of the function gets closer to zero but never reaches it.

wrong.0: The function values remain positive because the base is positive.
wrong.1: The graph approaches zero, not one.
wrong.3: This would be the value when x equals zero.
